text: The phosphopeptides keep calcium and phosphate dissolved as tiny amorphous particles, which in a paste can top up the enamel surface. Lab-scale conditions from the Reynolds patent; the commercial process may differ.

links.name: Cross, Huq & Reynolds 2007, Curr Pharm Des

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.name: digest
steps.note: Trypsin at 0.2 % of the casein weight, in a 10 % casein solution, pH held at 8.0 with NaOH.

steps.name: clarify
steps.note: Acidified to pH 4.6 and the precipitate removed by centrifuge or microfilter, or microfiltered at pH 8.0 instead.
The supernatant is taken to pH 9.0, then CaCl₂ (1.6 M) and Na₂HPO₄ (1 M) are added slowly.
Keeps only the peptide–calcium phosphate complexes, by microfiltration and diafiltration.
